```{r}
###  VECM
                                                      ######################
                                                      

# Install/Load necessary libraries
                                                      
library(readxl)   # Import xlsx data
library(tseries)  # For ADF test
library(car)      # Choose lag in VAR
library(urca)     # For Johansen test
library(vars)     # For VECM wo SE
library(tsDyn)    # For VECM with SE for Alpha

                                                      
##########
##### Import data and clean/organize data
##########
                                                      
# D.CI <- read.csv("path_to_your_file/Data name.csv")
# or                                                       
# D.CI <- read_excel("path_to_your_file/Data name.xlsx", sheet='name of the sheet')
# D.CI = as.data.frame (D.CI); nrow(D.CI) # head(D.CI)                                           
                                                      
D.CI =  read_excel("Data_World_Development_Indicators.xlsx",sheet='tilR');
D.CI = as.data.frame (D.CI); nrow(D.CI) # head(D.CI)                                           

D.CI1 = D.CI[D.CI[,4]%in%c('EN.GHG.CO2.MT.CE.AR5','NE.GDI.TOTL.KD','NY.GDP.MKTP.KD'), ]; nrow(D.CI)
D.CI1[,1]=D.CI1[,3]=NULL

varialbe = as.factor(D.CI1[,2]); levels(varialbe)
levels(varialbe) = c('CO2','Fin','GDP')                                                    
D.CI1[,2] = varialbe

names(D.CI1) = c('Country','Series',c(1960:2023))# str(D.CI1)

D.CI2 = reshape(D.CI1, direction ='long', varying=list (names(D.CI1)[3:ncol(D.CI1)] ), v.names = "v", idvar = c("Country",'Series'), timevar='Year', time=1960:2023)
D.CI3 = reshape(D.CI2, idvar=c("Country","Year"), v.names=c('v'), timevar=c("Series"),direction="wide") ;  # head(D.CI3)


################################################################################
##########
##### Choose a sample country - USA
##########
################################################################################

unique(D.CI3$Country)

Dat = D.CI3[D.CI3$Country=='USA',]; nrow(Dat) # select a country
    sort(Dat$Year)
Dat = Dat

Dat = Dat[Dat$v.CO2>0, ]; nrow(Dat)
Dat = Dat[Dat$v.GDP>0, ]; nrow(Dat)
Dat = Dat[Dat$v.Fin>0, ]; nrow(Dat)

unique(Dat$Year)

Year = Dat$Year
CO2 = log(Dat$v.CO2); summary(CO2)
FD = log(Dat$v.Fin); summary(FD)
GDP = log(Dat$v.GDP); summary(GDP)
GDP2 = GDP^2; summary(GDP2) # NEW: Squared GDP for EKC test


#$ ADF Test for stationary
####################

adf.test(CO2)
adf.test(FD)
adf.test(GDP)
adf.test(GDP2) # NEW: ADF for squared GDP


#$ Johansen Test
#################

#$ Johansen: CO2 and FD  # ?ca.jo()
J_test1 <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2,FD), type = "eigen", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test1)
J_test2 <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2,FD), type = "trace", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test2)


#$ Johansen: CO2 and GDP
J_test3 <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2,GDP), type = "eigen", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test3)
J_test4 <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2,GDP), type = "trace", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test4)


#$ Johansen: FD and GDP
J_test5 <- ca.jo(data.frame(FD,GDP), type = "eigen", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test5)
J_test6 <- ca.jo(data.frame(FD,GDP), type = "trace", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test6)


#$ Johansen: CO2, FD, and GDP

VARselect(data.frame(CO2,FD,GDP), lag.max = 10, type = "trend")$selection

J_test7 <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2,FD,GDP), type = "eigen", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test7)
J_test8 <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2,FD,GDP), type = "trace", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test8)


#$ NEW: Johansen: CO2, FD, GDP, and GDP2 (EKC Test)

VARselect(data.frame(CO2,FD,GDP,GDP2), lag.max = 10, type = "trend")$selection

J_test9 <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2,FD,GDP,GDP2), type = "eigen", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test9)
J_test10 <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2,FD,GDP,GDP2), type = "trace", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test10)



#$ VECM Function CO2 and FD
#################

Vecm2 = VECM(data.frame(CO2,FD), lag = 1, r=1, estim = "ML",include=c('const') )# ?VECM()
summary(Vecm2)

#$ long-run, beta

round(Vecm2$model.specific$beta,3)
cov = cov( residuals (Vecm2))
t_stats <- Vecm2$model.specific$beta / sqrt(diag(cov))
p_values <- 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stats), df = length(CO2) - 2))
p_values

#$ short-run, alpha

round ( summary(Vecm2)$coefMat, 3)


#$ VECM for CO2, FD, and GDP
#################

Vecm2 = VECM(data.frame(CO2,FD,GDP), lag = 1, r=1, estim = "ML",include=c('const') )# ?VECM()
summary(Vecm2)

#$ long-run, beta

round(Vecm2$model.specific$beta,3)
cov = cov( residuals (Vecm2))
t_stats <- Vecm2$model.specific$beta / sqrt(diag(cov))
p_values <- 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stats), df = length(CO2) - 2))
p_values

#$ short-run, alpha

round ( summary(Vecm2)$coefMat, 3)


#$ NEW: VECM for CO2, FD, GDP, and GDP2 (EKC Test)
#################

Vecm_EKC = VECM(data.frame(CO2,FD,GDP,GDP2), lag = 1, r=1, estim = "ML",include=c('const') )
summary(Vecm_EKC)

#$ long-run, beta

round(Vecm_EKC$model.specific$beta,3)
cov_ekc = cov( residuals (Vecm_EKC))
t_stats_ekc <- Vecm_EKC$model.specific$beta / sqrt(diag(cov_ekc))
p_values_ekc <- 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stats_ekc), df = length(CO2) - 2))
p_values_ekc

#$ short-run, alpha

round ( summary(Vecm_EKC)$coefMat, 3)



################################################################################
##########
##### Choose a sample country - CHINA
##########
################################################################################

Dat_CHN = D.CI3[D.CI3$Country=='CHN',]; nrow(Dat_CHN) # select China
    sort(Dat_CHN$Year)
Dat_CHN = Dat_CHN

Dat_CHN = Dat_CHN[Dat_CHN$v.CO2>0, ]; nrow(Dat_CHN)
Dat_CHN = Dat_CHN[Dat_CHN$v.GDP>0, ]; nrow(Dat_CHN)
Dat_CHN = Dat_CHN[Dat_CHN$v.Fin>0, ]; nrow(Dat_CHN)

unique(Dat_CHN$Year)

Year_CHN = Dat_CHN$Year
CO2_CHN = log(Dat_CHN$v.CO2); summary(CO2_CHN)
FD_CHN = log(Dat_CHN$v.Fin); summary(FD_CHN)
GDP_CHN = log(Dat_CHN$v.GDP); summary(GDP_CHN)
GDP2_CHN = GDP_CHN^2; summary(GDP2_CHN) # NEW: Squared GDP for EKC test


#$ ADF Test for stationary
####################

adf.test(CO2_CHN)
adf.test(FD_CHN)
adf.test(GDP_CHN)
adf.test(GDP2_CHN) # NEW: ADF for squared GDP


#$ Johansen Test
#################

#$ Johansen: CO2 and FD  # ?ca.jo()
J_test1_CHN <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN), type = "eigen", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test1_CHN)
J_test2_CHN <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN), type = "trace", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test2_CHN)


#$ Johansen: CO2 and GDP
J_test3_CHN <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2_CHN,GDP_CHN), type = "eigen", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test3_CHN)
J_test4_CHN <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2_CHN,GDP_CHN), type = "trace", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test4_CHN)


#$ Johansen: FD and GDP
J_test5_CHN <- ca.jo(data.frame(FD_CHN,GDP_CHN), type = "eigen", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test5_CHN)
J_test6_CHN <- ca.jo(data.frame(FD_CHN,GDP_CHN), type = "trace", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test6_CHN)


#$ Johansen: CO2, FD, and GDP

VARselect(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN,GDP_CHN), lag.max = 10, type = "trend")$selection

J_test7_CHN <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN,GDP_CHN), type = "eigen", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test7_CHN)
J_test8_CHN <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN,GDP_CHN), type = "trace", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test8_CHN)


#$ NEW: Johansen: CO2, FD, GDP, and GDP2 (EKC Test)

VARselect(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN,GDP_CHN,GDP2_CHN), lag.max = 10, type = "trend")$selection

J_test9_CHN <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN,GDP_CHN,GDP2_CHN), type = "eigen", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test9_CHN)
J_test10_CHN <- ca.jo(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN,GDP_CHN,GDP2_CHN), type = "trace", ecdet = c("const"), K = 2); summary(J_test10_CHN)



#$ VECM Function CO2 and FD
#################

Vecm2_CHN = VECM(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN), lag = 1, r=1, estim = "ML",include=c('const') )# ?VECM()
summary(Vecm2_CHN)

#$ long-run, beta

round(Vecm2_CHN$model.specific$beta,3)
cov_CHN = cov( residuals (Vecm2_CHN))
t_stats_CHN <- Vecm2_CHN$model.specific$beta / sqrt(diag(cov_CHN))
p_values_CHN <- 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stats_CHN), df = length(CO2_CHN) - 2))
p_values_CHN

#$ short-run, alpha

round ( summary(Vecm2_CHN)$coefMat, 3)


#$ VECM for CO2, FD, and GDP
#################

Vecm3_CHN = VECM(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN,GDP_CHN), lag = 1, r=1, estim = "ML",include=c('const') )# ?VECM()
summary(Vecm3_CHN)

#$ long-run, beta

round(Vecm3_CHN$model.specific$beta,3)
cov3_CHN = cov( residuals (Vecm3_CHN))
t_stats3_CHN <- Vecm3_CHN$model.specific$beta / sqrt(diag(cov3_CHN))
p_values3_CHN <- 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stats3_CHN), df = length(CO2_CHN) - 2))
p_values3_CHN

#$ short-run, alpha

round ( summary(Vecm3_CHN)$coefMat, 3)


#$ NEW: VECM for CO2, FD, GDP, and GDP2 (EKC Test)
#################

Vecm_EKC_CHN = VECM(data.frame(CO2_CHN,FD_CHN,GDP_CHN,GDP2_CHN), lag = 1, r=1, estim = "ML",include=c('const') )
```

```{r}
#$ Plotting the EKC Curve and Finding the Turning Point (USA)
#############################################################

# 1. Extract the long-run coefficients (betas) from the VECM
# tsDyn orders these as: [1] CO2, [2] FD, [3] GDP, [4] GDP2
betas_USA <- Vecm_EKC$model.specific$beta

# 2. Flip the signs to isolate CO2 on the left side of the equation
beta_GDP_USA  <- -betas_USA[3] 
beta_GDP2_USA <- -betas_USA[4]

cat("GDP Coefficient (b1):", beta_GDP_USA, "\n")
cat("GDP Squared Coefficient (b2):", beta_GDP2_USA, "\n")

# For the EKC to exist, b1 should be positive and b2 should be negative.

# 3. Calculate the Turning Point
# The formula for the peak of a parabola is: -b1 / (2 * b2)
turning_point_USA <- -beta_GDP_USA / (2 * beta_GDP2_USA)
cat("The GDP turning point (in log form) is:", turning_point_USA, "\n")
cat("The GDP turning point (in absolute value) is:", exp(turning_point_USA), "\n")

# 4. Plot the Curve
# Create a sequence of GDP values from the minimum to the maximum in your sample
gdp_seq_USA <- seq(min(GDP), max(GDP), length.out = 100)

# Calculate the partial predicted CO2 based ONLY on GDP and GDP squared 
# (holding FD constant to visualize just the GDP-CO2 relationship)
co2_predicted_USA <- (beta_GDP_USA * gdp_seq_USA) + (beta_GDP2_USA * (gdp_seq_USA^2))

# Generate the plot
plot(gdp_seq_USA, co2_predicted_USA, 
     type = "l", 
     col = "blue", 
     lwd = 2,
     main = "Environmental Kuznets Curve (USA)",
     xlab = "Log of GDP",
     ylab = "Partial Effect on Log of CO2")

# Add a vertical line to show where the turning point occurs
abline(v = turning_point_USA, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend=c("EKC Curve", "Turning Point"), col=c("blue", "red"), lty=c(1,2), lwd=2)

```

```{r}

betas_USA <- Vecm_EKC$model.specific$beta
beta_GDP_USA  <- -betas_USA[3] 
beta_GDP2_USA <- -betas_USA[4]
turning_point_USA <- -beta_GDP_USA / (2 * beta_GDP2_USA)

usadf <- data.frame(GDP_USA = GDP, CO2_USA = CO2, beta_GDP_USA = beta_GDP_USA, beta_GDP2_USA = beta_GDP2_USA)
gdp_seq_USA <- seq(min(GDP), max(GDP), length.out = 100)
co2_predicted_USA <- (beta_GDP_USA * gdp_seq_USA) + (beta_GDP2_USA * (gdp_seq_USA^2))

usadf <- usadf %>% 
  mutate(co2_predicted_USA = (beta_GDP_USA * GDP) + (beta_GDP2_USA * (GDP^2)))



# ==========================================
# PLOT 2: CHINA
# ==========================================
betas_CHN <- Vecm_EKC_CHN$model.specific$beta
beta_GDP_CHN  <- -betas_CHN[3] 
beta_GDP2_CHN <- -betas_CHN[4]
turning_point_CHN <- -beta_GDP_CHN / (2 * beta_GDP2_CHN)


chinadf <- data.frame(GDP_CHN = GDP_CHN, CO2_CHN = CO2_CHN, beta_GDP_CHN = beta_GDP_CHN, beta_GDP2_CHN = beta_GDP2_CHN)

chinadf <- chinadf %>% 
  mutate(co2_predicted_CHN = (beta_GDP_CHN * GDP_CHN) + (beta_GDP2_CHN * (GDP_CHN^2)))


library(tidyverse)

usadf %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = GDP, y = co2_predicted_USA)) +
     geom_line(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
     geom_vline(xintercept = turning_point_USA, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
     labs(title = "EKC (USA)", x = "Log of GDP", y = "Partial Effect on Log of CO2") +
     theme_bw() +
     theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
     annotate("text", x = turning_point_USA, y = max(co2_predicted_USA), label = "Turning Point", color = "red", vjust = -1, size = 3.5)



chinadf %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = GDP_CHN, y = co2_predicted_CHN)) +
     geom_line(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
     geom_vline(xintercept = turning_point_CHN, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
     labs(title = "EKC (China)", x = "Log of GDP", y = "Partial Effect on Log of CO2") +
```

```{r}
# 1. Create a theoretical sequence that goes far enough left to see the turning point (e.g., from 25 to 31)
gdp_seq_theoretical_USA <- seq(25, 31, length.out = 200)

# 2. Build a new dataframe for plotting the curve
usadf_plot <- data.frame(
  GDP_Seq = gdp_seq_theoretical_USA,
  co2_predicted_USA = (beta_GDP_USA * gdp_seq_theoretical_USA) + (beta_GDP2_USA * (gdp_seq_theoretical_USA^2))
)


usadf_plot %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = GDP_Seq, y = co2_predicted_USA)) +
     # Add a shaded box to show where the actual USA data (1960-2023) sits
     annotate("rect", xmin = min(GDP), xmax = max(GDP), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
              alpha = 0.2, fill = "green") +
     annotate("text", x = 30, y = min(usadf_plot$co2_predicted_USA), 
              label = "Actual Data\nRange", color = "darkgreen", size = 3.5) +
     
     # Draw the curve and turning point
     geom_line(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
     geom_vline(xintercept = turning_point_USA, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
     labs(title = "EKC (USA) - Theoretical Curve vs Observed Data", 
          x = "Log of GDP", 
          y = "Partial Effect on Log of CO2") +
     theme_bw() +
     theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
     annotate("text", x = turning_point_USA, y = max(usadf_plot$co2_predicted_USA), 
              label = "Turning Point (25.7)", color = "red", vjust = -1, hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5)
```
